bug_semantics: An authenticated caller could invoke report.get with only an arbitrary reportId. protectedProcedure authenticated the caller, but enforceAccess checked project or organization membership only when raw input contained a projectId or organizationId key, so this input triggered no tenant authorization. The handler then passed the attacker-controlled UUID to the unscoped getReportById service, whose Prisma findUnique selected solely by id and returned the transformed report, disclosing another organization's projectId, event series, filters, breakdowns, formulas, and other saved configuration.
flaw_origin: PR #211 member commit 3540c8b83a57ca2f926725158defce34bf304fec first connected the pre-existing unscoped getReportById helper to a new protected report.get RPC whose schema carried reportId but no access-bearing projectId or organizationId. That nine-line endpoint in packages/trpc/src/routers/report.ts:138-146 completed the vulnerable cross-tenant path; its direct parent had neither the endpoint nor its getReportById import. GitHub later squash-merged the PR as 81a7e5d62ec29ad3bf971610d5243a11a62a603d, but the reconstructable member commit, not the aggregate, is the smallest BIC.
ai_marker: absent — the BIC commit object (git cat-file -p 3540c8b83a57ca2f926725158defce34bf304fec) names author and committer Carl-Gerhard Lindesvärd <lindesvard@gmail.com>, has the message body exactly `wip`, and has no trailers; there is no bot identity, Co-Authored-By trailer, Generated-with trailer, or other commit-object AI marker.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/Openpanel-dev/openpanel/security/advisories/GHSA-9x7c-f87x-2243 identifies report.get, packages/trpc/src/trpc.ts enforceAccess, and packages/db/src/services/reports.service.ts getReportById; it declares OpenPanel API 2.2.0 affected and 2.3.0 patched and records live validation at e8a0602cda5a4d4b463f11d298a1b078c446bf33. At the reconstructed BIC, packages/trpc/src/routers/report.ts:138-146 accepts only reportId and returns getReportById(reportId); packages/trpc/src/trpc.ts:91-123 checks access only inside has('projectId', rawInput) and has('organizationId', rawInput); packages/db/src/services/reports.service.ts:84-95 performs db.report.findUnique({where:{id}}) and returns transformReport. `git log -L 184,192:packages/trpc/src/routers/report.ts a45bdb0f9372d8d4ef61f313b41142b63a2140e2` led to squash commit 81a7e5d62ec29ad3bf971610d5243a11a62a603d (PR #211). `git ls-remote origin refs/pull/211/head` resolved 330321405d2ba207cb1672d1d38a4f0cdac85ad8; that head and 81a7e5d62ec29ad3bf971610d5243a11a62a603d have the identical tree bd678581f1cc78a42ff07619c4bd7051c7c69cbb. In the PR-member history for report.ts, 3540c8b83a57ca2f926725158defce34bf304fec adds the entire vulnerable nine-line handler, while later member 6b2efdd19bb044be0c7d0bdde9db0a599cbe2466 adds layout procedures and leaves that handler unchanged. A zero-context diff from direct parent 68d194e8c6a1dd52913fb5fed4c01aa2fc27d823 to 3540c8b83a57ca2f926725158defce34bf304fec shows the handler and import as additions, and `git grep` for both `get: protectedProcedure` and `return getReportById(reportId)` in the direct-parent report.ts produced no match. The direct first-party fix is https://github.com/Openpanel-dev/openpanel/commit/0a51b6805eed0b3da8376175acd5fa3d26819cb6: packages/trpc/src/routers/report.ts changes report.get to load the report, reject a missing report, call getProjectAccess with ctx.session.userId and report.projectId, reject absent access, and only then return the report. Version cross-check: the repository has no 2.2.0/2.3.0 git tag, but publisher registry records at https://hub.docker.com/v2/repositories/lindesvard/openpanel-api/tags/2.2.0 and https://hub.docker.com/v2/repositories/lindesvard/openpanel-api/tags/2.3.0 exist, and their BuildKit provenance names this GitHub repository and source revisions ed8b5c667e6dd7f7b960c60ea5be9ce8c11ad8e1 and 373be136190aa73debd4508fa4ac05619ce04a53 respectively. Revision ed8b5c667e6dd7f7b960c60ea5be9ce8c11ad8e1 contains the vulnerable direct return at report.ts:175-183, contains squash 81a7e5d62ec29ad3bf971610d5243a11a62a603d, and predates the fix; revision 373be136190aa73debd4508fa4ac05619ce04a53 contains 0a51b6805eed0b3da8376175acd5fa3d26819cb6 and has the access check at report.ts:197-215. Finally, the BIC commit-object-only attribution check found only the human author/committer and `wip` message described in ai_marker.
reasoning: The vulnerability is created by the composition of three facts: the new RPC accepts no tenant-scoped input, generic middleware therefore performs no membership lookup, and the service lookup is global by report UUID. The direct parent proves the externally callable composition did not yet exist. Mainline line history initially points to the large PR #211 squash, but the surviving public pull-request head reconstructs exactly the squash tree; examining the member history isolates 3540c8b83a57ca2f926725158defce34bf304fec as the commit that actually wrote the flawed handler, with 6b2efdd19bb044be0c7d0bdde9db0a599cbe2466 merely carrying it forward. The aggregate 81a7e5d62ec29ad3bf971610d5243a11a62a603d transported those lines to main and is present before the 2.2.0 image revision. Fix 0a51b6805eed0b3da8376175acd5fa3d26819cb6 closes the exact gap by deriving projectId from the fetched report and authorizing that project before disclosure; the 2.3.0 image revision contains this fix and the corrected code. Because the smallest BIC's own commit object has human author and committer identities and no AI authorship, co-authorship, generation trailer, or bot marker, later PR review automation and any evidence outside that BIC object do not attribute the root cause to AI, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
